idea: How to maintain a water tank
title: Preventing Sediment Build-Up in Water Tanks
description: An educational guide explaining how sediment settles in storage tanks and why flushing the bottom scour valve protects household plumbing.
image_prompt: Educational technical cutaway illustration of a vertical blue polyethylene water storage tank mounted on a clean outdoor concrete platform, 9:16 vertical composition. The cutaway reveals clear water inside with a distinct layer of dark silt and fine sand settled on the tank floor. Show physically realistic PPR and PVC pipe connections: an inlet pipe at the top, an overflow line near the upper rim, a main water supply outlet exiting the side wall 10 centimeters above the bottom floor, and a dedicated scour drain pipe with a brass ball valve positioned flush with the very bottom floor. Professional studio lighting, clean engineering rendering, realistic textures, empty space reserved at top and bottom for text overlay. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no fake brand labels, no impossible pipe joints.
visual_story: The viewer observes a clear sectional view of a water tank interior. The key feature is the height difference between the main water supply line (raised off the floor) and the bottom scour drain valve (flush with the floor). Settled silt sits safely below the supply line, visualising how regular bottom flushing prevents sediment from traveling into household taps.

on_image_text.hook: Why Sediment Accumulates in Water Tanks
on_image_text.explanation: Heavy solids settle to the tank floor, below the raised main supply outlet.
on_image_text.takeaway: Flush the bottom drain valve periodically to clear sediment before it reaches your supply pipes.
